Breastfeeding promotion (Direct evidence)
rows.explainer: We have not found any studies directly estimating the effect of breastfeeding promotion on economic outcomes.

rows.label: Weight (Direct evidence)
Breastfeeding promotion (Cognitive effects)
rows.explainer:
Based on uncertain evidence suggesting a moderate effect size (0.2 - 0.4 standard deviations). 

Kramer et al 2008 found that the large-scale Belarussian PROBIT trial led to large increases in both exclusive breastfeeding rates and cognitive measures: "The experimental intervention led to a large increase in exclusive breastfeeding at age 3 months (43.3% for the experimental group vs 6.4% for the control group; P < .001) and a significantly higher prevalence of any breastfeeding at all ages up to and including 12 months. The experimental group had higher means on all of the Wechsler Abbreviated Scales of Intelligence measures, with cluster-adjusted mean differences (95% confidence intervals) of +7.5 (+0.8 to +14.3) for verbal IQ, +2.9 (−3.3 to +9.1) for performance IQ, and +5.9 (−1.0 to +12.8) for full-scale IQ. " Kramer et al. 2008, Abstract, (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapsychi

rows.label: Weight (Cognitive effects)
Breastfeeding promotion (Growth)
rows.explainer:
Based on no substantial evidence of effect, or compelling evidence suggesting a precisely measured null effect.

Giugliani et al 2015 conducted a meta-analysis adding 16 studies to a previous review of 19 studies, and found that "the interventions had no impact on weight or length/height z scores [pooled effect: 0.03 (95% confidence interval: −0.06;0.12) and 0.03 (95% confidence interval: −0.02;0.08), respectively] and had a modest, but significant, reduction in body mass index/weight-for-height z scores [z score mean difference: −0.06 (95% confidence interval: −0.12;0.00)], which was limited to studies from low- and high-incomes settings." Giugliani et al 2015, Abstract
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/apa.13160

rows.label: Weight (Growth)
Breastfeeding promotion (Mortality)
rows.explainer:
Based on uncertain evidence suggesting a small effect size (<10% reduction) 

See calculations of breastfeeding promotion's mortality effect size on the "CEA" sheet here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QwHTuR7LghA5Pzz-Sj21nKzwmCmIzsGfui3o37cWuQw/edit#gid=761181935&range=A31:C33
